content.comment_body: Hello everyone, For a project involving 200 schools, I'm seeking advice on connecting a microphone to a [product_name] controller. My goal is to trigger an electric light organ or alarm using the analog threshold function. However, I'm struggling to find a microphone with a sufficiently strong output signal for the 0-10V analog input; most microphones, even when amplified, output too weak a signal. Can anyone suggest a microphone that can deliver a voltage range from 0 to approximately 5V?

Hi, I doubt you'll find a microphone with the output range you're looking for. Most microphones tend to have similar output characteristics. You might want to measure your microphone's output and design your own amplifier, or consider using standard signal converters (like PT100, 1000, TC to 0-10V). Standard converters might be an option. Hope this assists.

Hello, For your use case, a carbon microphone could work, though these are quite rare nowadays. I have a few in my laboratory, but nowhere near 200 units. You can learn more at [url]. You would connect the microphone in series with a resistor (value depending on your supply voltage) and utilize the voltage drop across it for detection. Best of luck!

Hello [user_name], Just sharing my solution – I use a solid state relay to transmit the signal to the [product_name] controller. The solid state relay connects to the speaker outputs of a small stereo system. As music plays, the relay activates and subsequently controls the [product_name] PLC. I use this setup for my holiday lights, programming patterns so each relay closure triggers movement. A rectifier and conventional DC relay could also work. In my setup, I used two stereos for separation (one for bass, one for treble), allowing distinct outputs – for example, different patterns for bass and treble signals. My solid state relay handles a 3–30 VAC/DC input and 100–230 VAC output, and adjusting the stereo volume changes the signal intensity. Enjoy experimenting, [user_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Community members are exploring practical solutions for connecting a microphone to a [product_name] controller using its analog input for sound-triggered automations. The primary challenge is that most commercial microphones output signals too weak for the controller's analog input range. Suggestions include designing custom amplification circuits or using alternative signal converters, as off-the-shelf microphones likely won't meet the voltage requirements.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is seeking a microphone with a direct 0–5V (or 0–10V) output that can connect to the [product_name] analog input, aiming to avoid using extra circuitry and make installation as simple as possible.
